thread:
alex_chang: Heads-up: trying to publish py/ts SDKs now. I've queued the artifacts and will kick the publish in ~2m. watching CI logs.
maria_nguyen: thanks — which dist-tags are we using for this cut? canary or staged?
alex_chang: canary for the TS package, staged (beta) for Py so we don't break downstream yet. dist-tags in the release checklist:
```
npm publish --tag canary
python -m twine upload --repository-url https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/ dist/* --sign
# then set dist-tag: npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@v1.8.0 canary
```
samir: deploy-bot just posted a dry-run and one credential warning popped up in the publish step (token nearing expiry). @deploy-bot any details?
deploy-bot: CI WARNING: PyPI API token expires in 6 days for user alex_chang. Recommend rotating before final GA publish. Link: https://ci.internal/tokens/1234 :warning:
jen_lopez: ok that's borderline. For canary fine, but if GA is scheduled next week we should rotate now. Maria, can you help rotate the PyPI key and update shiproom docs?
maria_nguyen: yep will rotate. I'll create a new PyPI token with limited scope and update repo secret immediately. tagging ops once done.
alex_chang: timeline: canary/py-staged publish goes out now. we'll verify telemetry and install smoke tests. GA cut depends on token rotation + a quick compatibility smoke.
samir: also saw a flaky test in JS integration that touches the signer helper — it failed once in CI. Not sure to block publish but should be monitored.
jen_lopez: let's proceed but leave GA gated. Publish canary/staged, flag telemetry. If signer test regressions show up we stop and yank the canary dist-tag.
alex_chang: doing the npm publish now.
ci-bot: npm publish dry-run passed for @redwood/sdk-js v1.8.0-canary. Artifacts at https://artifacts.internal/6167890123/npm
maria_nguyen: rotated PyPI token, updated SECRET_PYPI_TOKEN in repo, verified twine upload with test artifact.
alex_chang: executing twine upload to staged now.
ci-bot: twine upload succeeded for redwood-sdk-python v0.9.0-beta. Artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/6167890123/pypi
samir: smoke install+import checks passing on mac/linux. Node smoke passed on node 18/20.
alex_chang: pinging release-tracker with canary/staged and note: watch signer-helper test. adding rollback plan to the thread.
jen_lopez: rollback plan (short):
- npm: npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk latest; npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk previous-stable latest
- pypi: yanking release isn't straightforward; mark package as deprecated on PyPI and unpublish if critical (PyPI support req). Prefer to announce and push a patched beta then GA.
- CI: revert publish job commit that bumped dist-tags and secrets if needed.
samir: also add ops-level mitigation: route Canary traffic to dedicated shadow route in staging for 2h before GA switch.
maria_nguyen: token rotation ok. FYI I truncated token expiry notes in shiproom docs and added a rotation checklist.
alex_chang: we have telemetry hooks enabled. if error rate or signer-test flakiness > threshold (0.5% build fail or 3 reproducible failures) we run rollback.
jen_lopez: noted. I'll prepare release notes draft and deprecation blurb for the legacy sync client (we're deprecating sync client in next minor). Will attach link when done.
ci-bot: alert: signer-helper test failed 2x in a row on canary consumers
deploy-bot: marking thread:monitor for 30m. Rolling back dist-tag if further failures.
samir: observed an upstream dependency bump that might be correlated. Opening a quick PR to pin the transitive dep to previous patch.
alex_chang: ok hold on any GA release until we get 30m green. If failures continue we remove canary tag and re-run canary with pinned dep.
maria_nguyen: done with token rotation audit. also updated Secrets Manager to set rotation schedule 7 days.
jen_lopez: release notes draft: https://docs.internal/releases/sdk-1.8.0-canary-notes.md — includes deprecation note and upgrade guide for TS/Py. please add comments.
alex_chang: thanks everyone. current status: canary + staged published; monitoring window started. next update in ~25m or earlier if we hit threshold. :eyes:
